title: ProfileDraft
description: Single JSON contract emitted by extract(); rendered deterministically by render().

type.description: How the source reached us. `paste` is a synonym of `text` that live models emit unprompted; agent/onboard/knowledge.py:_source_label treats both as 'manual' provenance.

slug.description: Kebab-case profile slug. 1-40 chars. Output of slugify().

markets.description: Empty is a legitimate answer: the prompt tells the brain to leave what it could not obtain UNSET and list it under `gaps` rather than infer it.

bucket.description: Optional competitive category this rival belongs to, e.g. 'Direct rivals', 'Adjacent tech', 'Incumbents', 'Status-quo / DIY'. Lets render() group competitors into tiers instead of one flat list. Free text — use the buckets that actually describe this market.

brand.description: Brand material as body_template.md's `### brand` section asks for it. Nothing here is required: that section's standing rule is to obtain rather than infer, and to leave what could not be obtained UNSET and listed under `gaps` — a fabricated logo and an invented palette have both shipped from this repo. Sub-shapes are deliberately unpinned because the prompt does not pin them either; the closed key set is what this object enforces.

palette.description: Colour ROLES (canvas, surface, ink, primary, accent, rule, plus a light-mode set) as an object, per the prompt. An array of hex codes is the older sampled-from-the-site form and still renders. `null` records that no palette was obtainable.

brand_document.description: The brand guideline / design-system document, if one exists. `null` is a real answer, not a gap.

sub_brand_map.description: Which product maps to which sub-brand/suite; records confirmed absences too.

typography.description: Display face, body face, and the role restriction between them.

logo_files.description: The logo pack by lockup and background, plus clear-space/minimum-size rules. Never generated or approximated.

mode_default.description: Dark-first or light-first, and which asset types invert it.

imagery.description: The house look as prompt text, plus hard rejects and soft avoids.

accessibility.description: Contrast rules, any no-meaning-by-colour-alone rule, an alt-text template.

pronunciation.description: How the company name is said, one respelling.

buyer_journey.description: Optional. The 'why now, where in the journey, and what moves them' layer — derived from the personas and whatever industry/market context is in the source. Everything here is inferred (the real answers only the seller knows), so each derived item should also surface in operator_confirm[] for the review gate. Absent = render() ships a persona-derived skeleton the operator fills in.

primary_persona.description: The persona title whose full journey the `stages` array describes — normally the primary economic buyer. Should match one of icp.personas[].title.

triggers.description: Trigger events ('why now') that time an outreach touch, roughly ranked by how strongly each predicts a buy.

event.description: The observable event, e.g. 'New aircraft type induction / large fleet order'.

activates.description: The persona this trigger most activates (a persona title).

predicts.description: Why this event predicts a buy — the opening it creates.

detect_via.description: How to detect it, free web first then a connected feed, e.g. 'OEM order press, careers page → RocketReach hiring signal'.

stages.description: The buyer journey for the primary_persona — one row per stage (e.g. Unaware → Problem-aware → Solution-aware → Vendor-aware → Evaluation → Decision → Expansion).

buyer_question.description: The question in the buyer's head at this stage.

angle.description: The content angle that moves them forward.

proof.description: The proof they need to advance.

objection.description: The objection to pre-empt at this stage.

pillar.description: The content pillar / asset that serves this stage — ideally one of pillars[].

persona_deltas.description: For secondary personas, only where their journey differs from the primary — where they enter, what leads, their sharpest trigger and objection.

persona.description: Persona title (matches an icp.personas[].title). This is the key render_icp.py reads.

notes.description: How this persona's journey differs — entry stage, leading message, sharpest trigger, top objection. The prompt names these four as prose, not as fields, so a model may split them into keys of its own naming instead; both are accepted.

operator_confirm.description: Inferred items only the seller can truly confirm — real sales-cycle length, which trigger historically closes, who signs vs. who champions, the objections actually heard in the room. Surfaced at the review gate.

settings.description: Operator-supplied config from the interview. Optional; render() supplies defaults when absent.

connectors.description: Per-connector plan/entitlement facts, one entry per metered tool the operator connects. Generic across tools (Vibe, RocketReach, Firecrawl, ...) — not tool-specific. Distinct from the 'Tools connected' status-only block: this captures WHICH plan and HOW MUCH it allows, so a flat-subscription tool (cost_usd near 0 per call) can still be paced against a real monthly limit instead of only the dollar cap.

plan.description: Plan/tier name as the vendor names it, e.g. 'Ultimate + Phone', 'Boost pack'.

billing.description: How the plan is billed — governs whether the dollar cap or the monthly_allowance count is the real constraint.

monthly_allowance.description: The plan's real recurring limit, in the unit that actually matters for this tool (not always dollars).

features.description: Premium features this plan enables, e.g. 'intent', 'phone', 'api_access', 'signal_search'. A skill should gate a premium-only facet/call on its presence here rather than assuming it works.

notes.description: Free text for anything uncertain — mark CONFIRM if the operator wasn't sure of an exact number.

gaps.description: Fields the brain couldn't fill from the source. Empty = no gaps.
